openClinicalQuestions: Which antiemetic categories does Dr. Charmi want named for Indian readers beyond the generic ‘anti-sickness medicines’ phrasing?
Any FOGSI hyperemesis pathway details to add once verified?

claimLedger.claim: Symptoms any time of day; usually eases by 16–20 weeks; self-care diet/rest/ginger/acupressure; call if dark urine/not peed >8h, unable to keep fluids 24h, faint, pain, fever, blood in vomit, weight loss; antiemetics if needed
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Vomiting and morning sickness · Media last reviewed dates on page; content fetched this session
claimLedger.limitations: UK call pathways (111/GP/midwife); use local maternity/emergency contacts in India

claimLedger.claim: NVP affects up to 90%; onset before 16 weeks; morning sickness label inaccurate; HG affects 0.3–3.6% and interferes with eating and drinking
claimLedger.sourceSection: RCOG · The Management of Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy and Hyperemesis Gravidarum (Green-top Guideline No.69) · First edition; next review date 2027 (page statement)
claimLedger.limitations: UK clinical guideline landing page; full Wiley PDF not required for these prevalence/definition points
